propositions: Review-bot uvicorn access logs record full request lines including query string, exposing the webhook_token (which is GERRIT_BOT_TOKEN) to journald and any system that reads the journal.

The shared secret is used to authenticate both /webhook (called by Gerrit) and /rerun (operator-driven) endpoints via query parameter (?token=...), making it the Gerrit credential and board authorization token.
Leaked credentials in journald cannot be treated as unexposed; journal content flows to observability.sh greps, log excerpts shared in tickets/chat, and future log-shipping systems.

The fix moves the token out of the query string into the X-Rebar-Token HTTP header (not recorded in access logs) for both endpoints and installs a TokenRedactingFilter as a backstop to redact token= from any logged request line.
The previously-logged token must be rotated and that rotation explicitly tracked separately from the code fix, since the code fix does not un-leak what is already in journald.
Access logs must continue to record route and status for observability greps and debugging.
